news.title: Leandro Paredes sparks uproar for unsportsmanlike act weeks after World Cup final ‘punch’
news.lede: Argentina international Leandro Paredes has again caused an uproar after appearing to kick the ball at an opponent. The midfielder was at the centre of controversy in a hostile end to the World Cup final vs Spain. After the full-time whistle of Spain’s 1-0 extra-time win over Argentina, Paredes was involved in an incident in which he confronted opposition players. TV footage appears to show him throwing punches towards Gavi and throwing him to the ground.

news.title: Gianni Infantino was set to earn huge salary from World Cup plan as staggering figure revealed
news.lede: FIFA chief Gianni Infantino was reportedly set to pocket a staggering £47 million per year had his plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup succeeded. Infantino, 56, came under heavy fire after the failed unveiling of his plans to sell off fractions in FIFA competitions to private investors. The FIFA president's idea plunged the football world into chaos. However, he pulled off a dramatic U-turn after considerable backlash, with pressure now mounting on the Swiss and support for his re-election collapsing.

news.title: The women behind UEFA's stand against Infantino's World Cup sell-off
news.lede: UEFA vice-president Laura McAllister and Norwegian Football Federation president Lise Klaveness emerged as two of the leading figures behind European football's opposition to FIFA's abandoned World Cup investment proposal. Citing multiple sources familiar with UEFA's emergency meeting involving around 150 officials, The Athletic reported that McAllister was among the first senior figures to call for a full boycott of FIFA competitions if president Gianni Infantino pressed ahead with plans to sell a minority stake in the commercial rights of the World Cup through the proposed FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE). The report added that, apart from UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin, no officials were more vocal in calling for decisive action than McAllister and Klaveness.

news.title: Crushing blow for FIFA boss as first re-election domino falls
news.lede: Updated August 3, 2026 - 9.00am. First published at 8.13am. England is set to join Wales in formally withdrawing support for FIFA president Gianni Infantino’s bid for re-election after his attempt to sell off stakes in the World Cup. Support for Infantino has dwindled since his proposal of a FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) that would act as a commercial subsidiary to run FIFA events like the World Cup and Club World Cup.
